meta.name: Kanopy Security
meta.title: Kanopy Security ad teardown: a free assessment that turns into a demo
meta.meta_desc: A teardown of Kanopy Security’s live LinkedIn ad: it offers a free 90-day Shadow AI assessment, then the landing page only offers “Book a demo” and shows no customer proof.
meta.og_desc: A free assessment in the ad. A demo on the page.
meta.keywords: kanopy security linkedin ads, kanopy ad teardown, shadow AI ads, AI governance ads, offer mismatch, ad teardown
meta.card_desc: The ad offers a free 90-day assessment. The page only offers “Book a demo.”

hook: The ad offers a free assessment.
The page only offers a demo.
voice.lede: “Overprivileged Agents Are Your Next Breach” is a hook built for the buyer, and a free 90-day Shadow AI assessment is a real reason to click. Then the offer disappears. The landing page says “Book a demo” everywhere, swaps the breach fear for “Smart AI Governance. Zero Friction.”, and shows no customer logos to a security buyer about to take a meeting.

findings.title: A threat list in the buyer’s words
findings.what: “Hardcoded Secrets. Overprivileged Agents. Suspicious Skills.” is specific language this buyer uses every day. It frames the threat before it sells anything.

findings.title: Two threat lists at once
findings.what: The body leads with overprivileged agents and the creative leads with hardcoded secrets and suspicious skills. The two run in parallel instead of building on each other.
findings.fix: Pick one threat and carry it through the copy, the creative and the page.

findings.title: No proof anywhere in the ad
findings.what: No named customer, no logo, no analyst mention and no number. A free assessment still asks a security team to let a new vendor in.
findings.fix: Add one named customer or one finding from a real assessment.

findings.title: The offer disappears
findings.what: The ad promises a free 90-day assessment. The page says “Book a demo” everywhere, which is a different ask with more friction.
findings.fix: Make the assessment the page’s only CTA, in the same words as the ad.

findings.title: The hook is dropped in the headline
findings.what: “Smart AI Governance. Zero Friction.” is category language. It leaves behind the breach fear that earned the click, and the tone moves to “Marie Kondo for your AI jungle.”
findings.fix: Open with “Overprivileged Agents Are Your Next Breach,” then show how the assessment finds them.

findings.title: No proof on the page either
findings.what: Zero customer logos, case studies, certifications or named enterprise users, in front of a buyer at a large enterprise.
findings.fix: Put one piece of proof above the fold, next to the CTA.

faq.q: What is wrong with Kanopy Security’s LinkedIn ad?
faq.a: The ad is strong. The problem is the handoff: it offers a free 90-day Shadow AI assessment and the landing page only offers “Book a demo.”

faq.q: Why does changing the CTA after the click hurt?
faq.a: The buyer clicked for one offer and is asked for a bigger commitment. A free assessment and a sales demo are different decisions, so the click has to be earned again.

faq.q: How would you fix this page?
faq.a: Repeat the ad’s headline, make the assessment the only CTA, and add one piece of customer proof above the fold.

issues.title: Headline Clarity
issues.explanation: 'Hardcoded Secrets. Overprivileged Agents. Suspicious Skills.' is punchy and specific jargon this buyer actually uses daily. Clear threat framing.

issues.title: CTA Friction
issues.explanation: 'Find Them All' is a fun but vague button for a security assessment; the ad body's 'Get a free 90-day assessment' is clearer than the creative's CTA.

issues.title: Visual-Copy Match
issues.explanation: Ad body text ('Overprivileged Agents Are Your Next Breach') doesn't fully match creative headline ('Hardcoded Secrets, Suspicious Skills'), two different threat lists running in parallel.

issues.title: Benefit Specificity
issues.explanation: 'Detect over-permissioned agents, embedded business data, and public exposure, automatically' is concrete, but 'automatically' and '90-day assessment' lack a quantified outcome or finding.

issues.title: Trust Signals
issues.explanation: No named customer, logo, analyst mention or number anywhere in the ad; LinkedIn supports image-based trust signals and this creative skips them entirely.
